summary: Return the squares of a non-decreasing array sorted in non-decreasing order.
mainInsight: The largest square is at one of the ends. Use two pointers at both ends and fill the result from the back, taking the larger square each time and moving that pointer inward. This is O(n) instead of squaring and sorting in O(n log n).

approaches.name: Square then sort
approaches.summary: sorted(x * x for x in nums).

approaches.name: Two pointers from both ends
approaches.summary: Fill the result from the end with the larger square.

commonMistakes: Using absolute values in the wrong order
Forgetting that all-negative or all-positive arrays are valid

promptVariants: Why does the largest square always lie at one of the two ends?
options: Large-magnitude negatives square to large values, so a maximum sits at an end
The largest square is always the last element
The largest square always sits in the array's middle
The largest square belongs to the value nearest zero
cards.answer: Large-magnitude negatives square to large values, so a maximum sits at an end
cards.explanation: The array is sorted by value, not by absolute value.

incorrectOptionExplanations.The largest square is always the last el: A large negative at the front can be larger in magnitude.
incorrectOptionExplanations.The largest square always sits in the ar: Near zero the squares are smallest.

promptVariants: Why fill the result from the back?
What would happen if you filled it from the front?
cards.answer: The pointers at the ends give the largest remaining square, so each step determines the next largest value. Filling from the front would need the smallest square, which lies in the middle near zero and requires a different pointer strategy.
cards.explanation: Alternative: start at the sign change and merge outward.

promptVariants: Complete the statement: Space complexity (excluding the input): ___

options: [16, 1, 0, 9, 100]: the squares in the original order
[1, 0, 9, 16, 100]: the sign change is not handled
cards.explanation: Compare |-4| = 4 and 10; 100 is placed at the end.
